4.1.q: Requirements serve a dual function. At the detailed level they are the basis for:
4.1.vi: Mức cao: cơ sở cho đấu thầu/hợp đồng. Mức chi tiết: cơ sở cho team phát triển.
4.1.en: High level: basis for a bid or contract. Detailed level: basis for the development team.

4.1.q: Which is listed as a stakeholder type?
4.1.vi: 4 loại: end users, system owners, system managers, external stakeholders.
4.1.en: Types: end users, system owners, system managers, external stakeholders.

4.1.q: In the ATM example, which is listed as a stakeholder?
4.1.vi: Stakeholder ATM gồm khách hàng, ngân hàng khác, quản lý, nhân viên quầy, DBA, bảo mật, marketing, bảo trì, cơ quan quản lý ngân hàng.
4.1.en: ATM stakeholders include customers, other banks, managers, counter staff, DBAs, security, marketing, maintenance, banking regulators.

4.1.q: Stakeholders who do not use the system themselves but influence the requirements form which viewpoint?
4.1.vi: Interactor: tương tác trực tiếp · Indirect: không dùng nhưng ảnh hưởng · Domain: đặc điểm lĩnh vực.
4.1.en: Interactor: direct · Indirect: don't use but influence · Domain: domain characteristics.

o: In natural language, from the user's point of view
4.2.vi: User req: mức cao, ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, góc nhìn người dùng.
4.2.en: User requirements: high level, natural language, user's view.

4.2.q: System requirements are mainly written for:
4.2.vi: System req: góc nhìn kỹ thuật (designer, implementer, tester), định nghĩa cái cần hiện thực.
4.2.en: System requirements: technical view (designer, implementer, tester); what to implement.

4.2.q: "Passwords must be at least 8 characters, contain at least one number, and be encrypted when stored" is an example of a:
4.2.vi: Đây là system requirement chi tiết hoá user requirement "không muốn mật khẩu dễ đoán".
4.2.en: This system requirement details the user requirement "password not easily guessed".

4.3.q: Requirements that state how the system should react to particular inputs are:
4.3.vi: Functional: phản ứng với input, hành xử trong tình huống cụ thể.
4.3.en: Functional: reactions to inputs and behavior in situations.

4.3.q: Which property of good functional requirements is about having no contradictions?
4.3.vi: Precision: không mơ hồ · Completeness: đủ mọi chức năng · Consistency: không mâu thuẫn.
4.3.en: Precision: unambiguous · Completeness: all facilities · Consistency: no contradictions.

4.3.q: Usability, security and performance belong to which NFR type?
4.3.vi: Product: performance, security, usability, reliability… Organizational: delivery, implementation, standards. External: ethical, privacy, safety.
4.3.en: Product: performance, security, usability… Organizational: delivery, implementation, standards. External: ethical, privacy, safety.

o: Being easily transferred to different hardware or software environments
4.3.vi: Portability: dễ chuyển sang môi trường phần cứng/phần mềm khác. Compliance: tuân thủ luật, chuẩn.
4.3.en: Portability: easy transfer to other environments. Compliance: laws and standards.

4.3.q: Which statement about non-functional requirements matches the lecture?
o: They may be more critical than functional requirements
They are always less important than functional requirements
They only concern the user interface
4.3.vi: NFR có thể quan trọng hơn functional requirement.
4.3.en: NFRs may be more critical than functional requirements.

4.3.q: "The system should be easy to use by experienced controllers" is:
o: A goal, not yet a verifiable requirement
4.3.vi: Đây là goal. Bản verifiable: dùng được mọi chức năng sau 2 giờ đào tạo, ≤ 2 lỗi/ngày.
4.3.en: This is a goal. Verifiable: all functions after 2 hours training, ≤ 2 errors/day.

4.3.q: Which measure is listed for the property "Ease of use"?
4.3.vi: Ease of use: training time, số khung help. Reliability: MTTF, availability. Speed: transactions/second.
4.3.en: Ease of use: training time, help frames. Reliability: MTTF, availability. Speed: transactions/second.

4.3.q: "Because of copyright restrictions, some documents must be deleted immediately on arrival" is a:
4.3.vi: Domain requirement đến từ lĩnh vực (ví dụ library: Z39.50, bản quyền).
4.3.en: Domain requirements come from the domain (library: Z39.50, copyright).

4.3.q: In the NFR measures table, the reliability measure MTTF stands for:
4.3.vi: MTTF = Mean time to failure (thời gian trung bình tới khi hỏng), một thước đo của Reliability.
4.3.en: MTTF = Mean time to failure, a measure of reliability.

4.4.q: In the lecture's RE process, what comes right after the feasibility study?
4.4.vi: Feasibility study → Gathering → Specification → Validation; Management xuyên suốt.
4.4.en: Feasibility study → Gathering → Specification → Validation; management throughout.

4.4.q: Which is listed as a problem of requirements gathering?
o: Stakeholders don't know what they really want
Stakeholders always agree with each other
Developers know the domain better than users
4.4.vi: Khó khăn: không biết mình muốn gì, dùng ngôn ngữ riêng, mâu thuẫn, chính trị, requirement thay đổi.
4.4.en: Problems: don't know what they want, own terms, conflicts, politics, changing requirements.

4.4.q: Grouping related requirements into coherent clusters is which gathering activity?
4.4.vi: Discovery → Classification & organization → Prioritization & negotiation → Documentation.
4.4.en: Discovery → Classification & organization → Prioritization & negotiation → Documentation.

4.4.q: In MoSCoW, "the release fails without it" describes:
4.4.vi: Must: thiếu thì release thất bại · Should: quan trọng, có workaround · Could: có thì tốt · Won't: để lại lần này.
4.4.en: Must: release fails without it · Should: workaround exists · Could: nice to have · Won't: left out this time.

4.4.q: In the course registration example, "Suggest courses from the study plan" is:
4.4.vi: Ví dụ: Must = đăng ký, chặn trùng lịch · Should = danh sách chờ · Could = gợi ý môn · Won't = mobile app.
4.4.en: Must = register, no conflicts · Should = waiting list · Could = suggest courses · Won't = mobile app.

4.4.q: Which is a limitation of interviewing?
o: It takes the client's time and schedule
It may interfere with the client's business
4.4.vi: Interview: tốn thời gian của khách, khó kiểm soát, khó lấy chi tiết. Observe: tốn thời gian dev, làm phiền khách.
4.4.en: Interview: costs client time, hard to control and to get details. Observe: costs dev time, interferes.

4.4.q: A question with limited possible answers in an interview is:
4.4.vi: Closed: đáp án giới hạn. Open: không giới hạn.
4.4.en: Closed: limited answers. Open: unlimited answers.

4.4.q: Facilitated sessions where stakeholders and developers work together are called:
4.4.vi: JAD workshops: stakeholder và developer làm việc chung có điều phối. Nên kết hợp nhiều kỹ thuật.
4.4.en: JAD workshops: facilitated joint sessions. Combine several techniques.

4.4.q: The capital letters in "MoSCoW" stand for:
o: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have (this time)
Must have, Should have, Can have, Will have
Must have, Should have, Could have, Wish to have
4.4.vi: MoSCoW = Must / Should / Could / Won't have (this time).
4.4.en: MoSCoW = Must / Should / Could / Won't have (this time).

4.5.q: Which specification method uses mathematical equations and programming languages?
4.5.vi: Natural: dễ viết nhưng mơ hồ · Structured: theo mẫu · Formal: toán, ngôn ngữ lập trình · Modeling: sơ đồ + form.
4.5.en: Natural: easy but ambiguous · Structured: a form · Formal: math, programming languages · Modeling: diagram + form.

o: The official statement of what is required of the system developers
An informal chat log with users
4.5.vi: SRS: tuyên bố chính thức; gồm user và system requirement; nói WHAT không HOW.
4.5.en: SRS: the official statement; user and system requirements; WHAT not HOW.

4.5.q: In Agile methods (Scrum, XP), the main requirements documents are:
o: A vision/objectives document and user stories
4.5.vi: RUP: Vision + use-case specs. Agile: Vision/objectives + user stories.
4.5.en: RUP: vision + use-case specs. Agile: vision/objectives + user stories.

4.5.vi: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.
4.5.en: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

4.5.q: In "Given the course is full, when I click Register, then I see 'Course is full'", the "Given" part states:
4.5.vi: Given: tình huống ban đầu · When: hành động · Then: kết quả mong đợi.
4.5.en: Given: starting situation · When: action · Then: expected result.

4.5.q: Which is a recommended precaution for AI-assisted requirements engineering?
o: Do not paste confidential or personal data into public AI tools
Use AI output as the final SRS
4.5.vi: Cẩn thận: AI có thể bịa requirement; luôn xác nhận với người dùng thật; người quyết định ưu tiên; không dán dữ liệu mật.
4.5.en: Careful: AI may invent requirements; validate with users; humans decide priorities; no confidential data.

4.5.vi: SRS = Software Requirements Specification: tuyên bố chính thức về những gì developer phải làm (WHAT, không phải HOW).
4.5.en: SRS = Software Requirements Specification: the official statement of what developers must build (WHAT, not HOW).

4.5.vi: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable. Bẫy: Traceable là chủ đề của traceability, không thuộc INVEST.
4.5.en: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable. Trap: traceable belongs to traceability, not INVEST.

o: Fixing requirements errors after delivery costs much more than fixing them early
It is only needed for agile projects
It removes the need for stakeholders
4.6.vi: Lỗi requirement gây lỗi design, code, test; sửa sau bàn giao tốn hơn nhiều.
4.6.en: Requirement errors spread into design, code, test; fixing after delivery costs far more.

4.6.q: "Are all functions required by the customer included?" is which check?
4.6.vi: Validity · Verifiability · Consistency · Completeness (đủ chức năng) · Realism.
4.6.en: Validity · Verifiability · Consistency · Completeness (all functions) · Realism.

4.6.q: Using an executable model of the system to check requirements is:
4.6.vi: Reviews: phân tích thủ công (phổ biến nhất) · Prototyping: mô hình chạy được · Test-case generation: viết test.
4.6.en: Reviews: manual analysis (most common) · Prototyping: executable model · Test-case generation: write tests.

4.6.q: Which statement about requirements reviews is correct?
o: They may be formal or informal and should involve analysts, designers, developers and testers
4.6.vi: Review thường xuyên, có analyst/designer/dev/tester, formal hoặc informal.
4.6.en: Regular reviews with analysts, designers, developers, testers; formal or informal.

4.7.q: Why are requirements inevitably incomplete and inconsistent?
o: New requirements emerge, business needs change and understanding improves
Engineers write them carelessly on purpose
4.7.vi: Requirement luôn thay đổi: nhu cầu mới, kinh doanh đổi, hiểu hệ thống hơn.
4.7.en: Requirements change: new needs, business change, better understanding.

4.7.q: Which is listed as a reason requirements change?
o: Business and technical environments change during the project
4.7.vi: Lý do: nhu cầu kinh doanh, hiểu rõ hơn, ưu tiên đổi, môi trường kinh doanh/kỹ thuật đổi.
4.7.en: Reasons: business needs, better understanding, priorities, environment changes.

4.7.q: Assessing the effects of a change on other requirements happens in:
4.7.vi: Change request → Change analysis and costing (đánh giá ảnh hưởng, chi phí) → Change implementation.
4.7.en: Change request → analysis and costing (effects, cost) → implementation.

4.7.q: In the traceability matrix example, FR-02 "Prevent timetable conflicts" is linked to:
4.7.vi: FR-02 → UC-03 Register → ScheduleChecker → TC-13. Ma trận dùng cho impact analysis và test coverage.
4.7.en: FR-02 → UC-03 Register → ScheduleChecker → TC-13. Used for impact analysis and test coverage.

4.7.q: In the traceability matrix, a row ID such as "NFR-01" identifies a:
4.7.vi: NFR = Non-functional requirement. Ví dụ NFR-01: tìm kiếm ≤ 1 s ở P95, được truy tới test PT-01.
4.7.en: NFR = Non-functional requirement. Example NFR-01: search in ≤ 1 s at P95, traced to test PT-01.
